title: The Winged Monkeys, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Suppose we call the field mice,” she suggested. “They could probably tell us the way to the Emerald City.”
“To be sure they could,” cried the Scarecrow. “Why didn’t we think of that before?”

Dorothy blew the little whistle she had always carried about her neck since the Queen of the Mice had given it to her. In a few minutes they heard the pattering of tiny feet, and many of the small gray mice came running up to her. Among them was the Queen herself, who asked, in her squeaky little voice:
“What can I do for my friends?”
“We have lost our way,” said Dorothy. “Can you tell us where the Emerald City is?”

“Certainly,” answered the Queen; “but it is a great way off, for you have had it at your backs all this time.” Then she noticed Dorothy’s Golden Cap, and said, “Why don’t you use the charm of the Cap, and call the Winged Monkeys to you? They will carry you to the City of Oz in less than an hour.”
“I didn’t know there was a charm,” answered Dorothy, in surprise. “What is it?”

“It is written inside the Golden Cap,” replied the Queen of the Mice. “But if you are going to call the Winged Monkeys we must run away, for they are full of mischief and think it great fun to plague us.”
“Won’t they hurt me?” asked the girl anxiously.
“Oh, no. They must obey the wearer of the Cap. Good-bye!” And she scampered out of sight, with all the mice hurrying after her.
Dorothy looked inside the Golden Cap and saw some words written upon the lining. These, she thought, must be the charm, so she read the directions carefully and put the Cap upon her head.
“Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!” she said, standing on her left foot.
“What did you say?” asked the Scarecrow, who did not know what she was doing.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy blow to call the mice?
options: The little whistle from the Queen
The Witch's silver whistle
A horn the Winkies gave her
Nothing; she called aloud

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Queen say about the Emerald City?
options: That it was a great way off, behind them all this time
That it lay only an hour's walk to the east
That she had never heard of such a place
That the road to it had been destroyed

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where is the charm of the Cap written?
options: Inside the Golden Cap, on the lining
On a slate the Queen carried
In a book in the Witch's cupboard
Nowhere; it must be remembered

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how long would the Monkeys take to carry them?
options: Less than an hour
A full day and night
About three days
Longer than walking

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the first words of the charm Dorothy said?
options: Ep-pe, pep-pe, kak-ke!
Hil-lo, hol-lo, hel-lo!
Ziz-zy, zuz-zy, zik!
She said nothing at all

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why must the mice run away before the Monkeys come?
options: The Monkeys are full of mischief and plague them
The Monkeys would eat them if they stayed
The Queen has quarrelled with the Monkey King
The charm only works if nobody else is near

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is Dorothy safe from the Monkeys?
options: They must obey whoever wears the Cap
The mark on her forehead protects her
The Queen has spoken for her
She is carrying the mice's whistle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what had Dorothy not known until now?
options: That the Golden Cap carried any charm at all
That the field mice could be called by whistle
That the Emerald City lay to the east
That the Winged Monkeys existed

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does plague us mean?
options: Pester and torment us
Make us fall ill
Hunt and eat us
Copy everything we do

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Small friends point the way and name a power she already wears
The mice refuse to help and hurry away again at once
Dorothy decides the Cap is far too dangerous to use
The party walks east and reaches the city on foot

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who came with the field mice?
options: The Queen herself
The Monkey King
The Guardian of the Gates
Nobody else

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Scarecrow say when the mice were suggested?
options: That they should have thought of it before
That the mice could not possibly know
That he would rather keep walking east
That the Queen had forgotten them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy do after reading the lining?
options: Put the Cap on her head and stood on her left foot
Handed the Cap to the Scarecrow so he could read it
Called the Queen of the Mice back to explain it
Put the Cap away in her basket for safekeeping

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the mice arrive?
options: With a pattering of tiny feet, within a few minutes
Slowly, over the course of a whole day
Carried on the backs of the Monkeys
One at a time, from different directions

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did the Scarecrow not understand?
options: What Dorothy was doing as she spoke the charm
Why the mice had run away so quickly
How the Queen knew where the city was
Where Dorothy had found the Golden Cap

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does anxiously convey about Dorothy's question?
options: She asked out of worry for her own safety
She asked eagerly, hoping for good news
She asked without much caring about the answer
She asked to change the subject

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A whistle brings help, and the help points to a better one
A whistle brings mice who refuse to answer any questions
Dorothy learns that the Emerald City has been destroyed
The Winged Monkeys arrive before the charm is finished
